headline: Approved adult-use marijuana sales at 45 Boulder Way and relocating a structure at 64 Mile Stretch Road.
summary: The owners of 64 Mile Stretch Road asked to move a non-conforming structure from 15 feet to 33 feet from the shoreline. An earlier approval from May 2025 expired after delays by DEP. The board also talked about which items staff can handle without the board and how to make waterfront houses less vulnerable.
decisions: Approved the minutes of October 7, 2026 unanimously.
Approved the Greatest Practical Extent determination for 64 Mile Stretch Road unanimously.
Waived full site plan review for 45 Boulder Way unanimously.
Approved the conditional use permit for adult-use marijuana retail at 45 Boulder Way unanimously.

PLANNING BOARD MEETING MINUTES 
October 21, 2026 
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance-Meeting brought to order at 6:00 PM 
2. Declaration of Quorum 
Planning Board: John McCurry, Matthew Sargent-Dubois, Chico Potvin, Rob Nicoll 
(Alternate Member) & Dylan Doughty (Alternate Member)  
Nicoll & Doughty to vote for Angers & Schaffer 
Staff: David Galbraith, Marin Stephens & Nan Whitten 
3. Adjustments to Agenda- Item 8a has been cancelled 
4. Planner’s Business 
• Staff Review Committee Meeting Minutes from 9-29-26 
• Galbraith introduced Marin Stephens, new Assistant Planner & Dylan Doughty 
Planning Board Member 
• Item 7b has been reversed applicant has a medical marijuana retail and is opening 
adult use. 
      5. Consent Agenda 
 5.a. Approval of Meeting Minutes of October 7, 2026  
 MOTIONS: 6:03PM 
 Motion- Potvin-Motion to approve Meeting Minutes as presented 
 Second-Sargen-Dubois 
 Vote: Motion passed unanimously 
6. Unfinished Business 
      7. New Business 
7.a 2026.46 The Planning Board will review a Shoreland Zoning Application by Dennis 
and Paula McNabb to relocate a non-conforming structure located at 64 Mile Stretch 
Road (Tax Map 61, Lot 17-1) in the Coastal Residential Zone. This project was 
previously approved by the Planning Board in May 2025, but delays by DEP caused the 
approval to expire. 
• Galbraith introduced the project.   
• Mike Morse from Archipelago represented the applicants 
• Previously approved in 2025 
• Remove and relocate a non-conforming structure GPE 
• 15’ from the shoreline to 33’  
• It cannot be relocated any further back for several reasons, small lot, no depth, 
40’city road setback that encumbers lot, existing driveway and septic 
• Application and plans are identical to previously approved.
• Doughty what caused the DEP delays, Morse-DEP said there are no issues, very 
little discussion, DEP has had staffing issues, applications are being delayed due 
to such issues, applications numbers are elevated, processing deadlines have 
been tossed out the door 
• Doughty-what is the current timeline for construction, Morse-they had hoped to 
start in September when they realized permit had expired, so as soon as possible 
• Nicoll, is it taller than the original house?  Morse, respectfully, that is not part of 
the PB purview but it is in compliance,  and Roby will review it thoroughly 
 
MOTIONS: 6:12 PM 
Motion- Nicoll- Motion to Approve Case #2026.46 A Greatest Practical Extent (GPE) 
Determination for Dennis McNabb and E. Paula McNabb of 64 Mile Stretch Road (Tax 
Map 61, Lot 17-1) in the Coastal Residential (CR) Zoning District with the below listed 
Conditions of Approval (COA):   
1. The razed building shall not be relocated closer to any of the existing property lines as 
noted on the approved plan. 
 
2. The Code Enforcement Officer shall review and approve conformance to Section 15 of 
the Shoreland Zoning Ordinance. 
 
3. Obtain all required permits from the Maine Department of Environmental Protection 
and the Biddeford Code Enforcement Office. 
 
4. This approval shall expire one year from the Planning Board approval date if a 
substantial start is not made in construction. If a substantial start (30% of project 
completion, i.e., framing and foundation) is made within one year of this approval (10-
21-2027), the applicant shall have one additional year to complete the project 
thereinafter; this approval shall expire. 
Second- Sargent-Dubois 
NO PUBLIC COMMENTS 
Vote- Motion passed unanimously 
 
7.b. 2026.47 The Planning Board will review a Conditional Use Permit Application by 
Blossom Retail, LLC to add adult-use marijuana sales to their existing location at 45 
Boulder Way (Tax Map 2, Lot 56) in the Industrial Zone 3. Blossom Retail currently runs 
and will continue to run a medical marijuana facility at this same location. 
• Galbraith introduced project 
• Operating a business for medical currently, seeking adult use retail in existing 
location.  
• Handicapped access has been added recently 
• Because it is an existing business & staying in the same structure it can be approved 
• There was a residential structure within 500’ but it has been torn down 
• Codes reports there are no complaints on this business
• McCurry confirmed that this is ok where it is within 1000 feet.  Old ordinance 
stated 500’ legal says it is ok to approve 
• Potvin expanding but changing use it was medical but now it is retail. 
• Elizabeth Baldacci representing the application 
• Baldacci is not expanding and she is using an additional license 
• Legal says marijuana is marijuana and it is the same. 
• Potvin feels it is a good operation 
• Doughty, does it have to be separated?  Baldacci, we do have to separate it left for 
one right for the other 
• Nicoll asked about traffic 
MOTIONS: 6:20 PM 
Motion-Nicoll- Motion to waive Article XI, full site plan review, as no site 
improvements are being made. 
Second-Sargent Dubois 
Vote-motion passed unanimously 
Motion-Nicoll-Motion to approve the Conditional Use Permit and the Findings of 
Fact and Conclusions of Law for Elizabeth Baldacci CEO for Blossom Cannabis for 
a Adult Use retail facility at 45 Boulder Way (Tax Map 2, Lot 56), with the attached 
Conditions of Approval. 
Second-Sargent Dubois 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
8. Open Public Hearing CANCELLED 
9. Close Public Hearing  
10. Other Business 
• Potvin-where are we on what items can be handled in house as opposed to the 
Board, Galbraith staff has already met on this topic 
• Nicoll-GPE requires more aggressive measures to preserve houses on the water so 
they are not as vulnerable.  Galbraith talked about options.  Potvin agrees but we 
must take a deep dive into that 
11. Adjourn 6:30 PM
